releaseClaim.userOperation: A participant at https://meet.know-me.tools shares a screen, chats with everyone or privately with one person, blurs or replaces their background, chooses and tunes microphone, camera and speaker, clicks 'Enable audio' when the browser blocks playback, records the meeting into their own browser after the room agrees, and after a reload finds past meetings, chats and recordings on the same device.
supportedEnvironments: Web only, hosted at https://meet.know-me.tools behind the existing gateway and continuous deployment
Current desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; controls a browser cannot support are hidden or explained
Phone browsers: chat, devices and history in layout; screen share and effects shown as unavailable where the browser cannot do them; media behaviour on phones not verified
Media: the existing LiveKit Cloud project
releaseClaim.currentCapabilities: Guest meetings with default devices; mute, camera, copy link and leave; nothing stored locally except session and theme; no recording; entity graph 4.3.0.
releaseClaim.desiredResult: Each operation works end to end on the hosted app. History and recordings survive a reload and never leave the device.

functionalScope: RealtimeRoom port extensions: screen share, text messages with explicit audience, devices including output, audio playback status and start, video processor hook; lobby device choice carried into the room
Recording consent use cases on a reserved text-stream topic
LiveKit adapter split into a feature directory implementing the extended port
Share control and tile, chat panel with audience labels, Enable audio prompt
Lobby and in-room device settings with level meter, preview and gated speaker choice
Hosted-only CSP widening with a desktop byte-identity guard and regenerated gateway header
Background blur and image backgrounds through @livekit/track-processors with self-hosted assets
Entity graph 5.0.1 from npm in the web app and both spikes
Local history in PGlite (idb://, leader worker) behind a HistoryRepository port and entity transports, with a history screen and delete
Browser-local composited recording into OPFS with consent, indicator, library and playback
Value scenarios WC-1 to WC-14 and their evidence
proposedDecisions: D1 Guests may use local history and local recording; PRODUCT.md 'Guest vs signed in' is amended accordingly
D2 Late joiner while recording: recording continues, the late joiner sees the indicator and a consent prompt; a decline stops the recording for everyone and keeps what was written
D3 No chat backfill to late joiners from anyone's local history
D4 The recording follows the room grid; a screen share takes the large tile
D5 Each device keeps the chat it received, others' messages included, locally only; the history screen says so and offers delete
requiredSafetyChecks: No recording starts without every present participant's consent, and everyone sees an indicator while it runs
Every chat message carries an explicit audience; a private message is delivered only to its named recipient
No secret in tracked files, the web bundle or the image; LIVEKIT_ values stay server-side
No history or recording data is sent to any server (network log check)
The CSP change applies to hosted output only; the desktop policy is byte-identical; WASM, model and worker files are served from 'self'
WCAG 2.2 AA, Flat 2.0 and reduced motion on every new control
riskAcceptance: Private chat passes through the LiveKit server and is readable there
Local history and recordings are lost when site data is cleared
Recordings are limited by browser storage quota
Composite and segmentation visual quality are judged from screenshots, not measured

scenarioMatrix.name: Screen share reaches the other participant and stops cleanly
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm --filter @know-meet/release-tests exec playwright test wc-1-screen-share.spec.ts --project=packaged, then --project=hosted
realCollaborators: Chromium with fake media and auto-accepted screen capture
scenarioMatrix.oracle: B reports a subscribed remote track with source ScreenShare whose rendered dimensions are greater than zero; after A stops, B reports no ScreenShare track within 10 s and A's share control returns to off.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: Without starting a share, B reports no ScreenShare track.
scenarioMatrix.evidence: Playwright report and trace, screenshots of both contexts, argv and exit code.

scenarioMatrix.name: A message to everyone reaches every participant
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: wc-2-chat-everyone.spec.ts, packaged then hosted; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
scenarioMatrix.oracle: With three participants, a message sent by A appears in B's and C's chat panels with text equal to the sent text and the audience label 'Everyone'.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: A message never sent does not appear anywhere.
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Three browser contexts, unique text per run.
scenarioMatrix.evidence: Report, trace, screenshots of all three panels.

scenarioMatrix.name: A private message reaches only its recipient
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: wc-3-chat-private.spec.ts, packaged then hosted; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
scenarioMatrix.oracle: A sends privately to B. B shows the text labelled private to B; A shows it labelled private to B; C's panel and C's received text-stream log never contain it after 10 s.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: The same run sends one Everyone message, which C does receive, proving C's listener was live.

scenarioMatrix.name: Blur and image backgrounds show remotely and turn off cleanly
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: wc-4-background-effects.spec.ts, packaged then hosted. Positive path: headed Chromium on the operator's Mac, whose WebGL renderer is hardware (ANGLE Metal); the run records the renderer string and fails BLOCKED if it reports a software renderer. Software path: headless Chromium as the rest of the suite runs it (SwiftShader).
realCollaborators: web image with self-hosted MediaPipe assets
scenarioMatrix.oracle: GPU path: after the effects section is shown and reports ready, choosing blur makes A's published track report an active processor and B's rendered frame differ from the pre-effect frame; after image, the same; after off, no processor and B still renders frames. After each choice, A's page answers a main-thread probe within 2 s (no unexplained freeze after the person chooses). No request leaves the origin for .wasm or .tflite files and no CSP violation is reported. Software path: the effects section states that background effects are not available on this device, the blur and image choices cannot be selected, A's track reports no processor, and A's mute control changes state within 2 s of a click.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With effects off, A's track reports no processor. On the software path, no processor is ever attached.
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Fake camera from a fixed y4m file; one fixture background image; a headed Chromium with hardware WebGL for the GPU path.
scenarioMatrix.evidence: Report, WebGL renderer string per path, frame screenshots (visual quality labelled judgement), main-thread probe timings, network log, CSP violation log, screenshot of the unavailable state.

scenarioMatrix.name: Chosen microphone and camera are the ones used
scenarioMatrix.oracle: The lobby lists the devices and shows a moving level and a preview; the device chosen in the lobby is the active device after join; switching in the room changes the active device id and B keeps receiving.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: Without a choice, the default device is active.
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Chromium fake media; device ids recorded per run.

scenarioMatrix.name: Speaker choice works where supported and is explained where not
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: wc-6-speaker.spec.ts, packaged; Chromium for selection, WebKit and Firefox for the explanation path
scenarioMatrix.oracle: Where setSinkId exists, choosing an output changes the active audiooutput device; where it is absent (forced by an init script removing it), the control is not offered and an explanation is visible and announced.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With setSinkId present, no explanation is shown.
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Init script for the unsupported path.

scenarioMatrix.name: History survives a reload and never leaves the device
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: wc-7-local-history.spec.ts, packaged then hosted; Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
scenarioMatrix.oracle: After a meeting with two chat messages and a reload, the history screen lists the meeting with its date and both messages; the network log for the whole run contains no request body or URL containing either message text or the history ids; deleting the entry removes it after another reload.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: A fresh browser profile shows an empty history.
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Persistent context per engine; unique message texts.

scenarioMatrix.name: A consented recording runs, saves locally and plays back
scenarioMatrix.oracle: A asks to record; B is prompted; after B agrees, both show the recording indicator; after 20 s A stops; A's library lists one recording with duration within 20 +/- 3 s and size greater than zero; it starts playing (currentTime advances); no network request carries recording bytes.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: Before B answers, no recording file exists and no indicator shows.
scenarioMatrix.evidence: Report, network HAR, file metadata, screenshots of both indicators.

scenarioMatrix.name: A declined consent means no recording
scenarioMatrix.oracle: A asks; B declines; A is told the request was declined; no indicator appears for anyone and A's library stays empty after 20 s. A late joiner C declining during a running recording stops it for everyone (decision D2).
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: WC-8 is the positive counterpart in the same run.
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Three contexts for the late-joiner case.

scenarioMatrix.name: The hosted page serves the new web CSP and nothing else is widened
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: headers.spec.ts and wr-3 checks extended, packaged then hosted; the desktop identity unit test in pnpm test
scenarioMatrix.oracle: The hosted HTML and worker .js responses carry a CSP equal to the generated hosted value, which differs from the previous one only by the adopted sources; .wasm is served as application/wasm; the tauri.conf.json csp equals the default policy byte for byte; WC-4, WC-7 and WC-8 report no CSP violation.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: The default (non-hosted) build's meta CSP has none of the new sources.
scenarioMatrix.evidence: Header captures, diff of old and new policy, unit test output.

scenarioMatrix.name: Entity graph 5.0.1 from npm, and notes still work
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm why @prometheus-ags/entity-graph-core in apps/web and both spikes; the existing notes scenario run against the packaged image
scenarioMatrix.oracle: The lockfile resolves entity-graph-core and -react to 5.0.1 with npm integrity hashes in all three packages; tooling/versions.toml says 5.0.1; the notes create-and-list flow passes.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: pnpm lint:pins fails if any package still pins 4.x or 5.0.0.
scenarioMatrix.evidence: pnpm why output, lockfile excerpt, notes report.

scenarioMatrix.name: Enable audio appears when autoplay is blocked and starts audio
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: wc-12-enable-audio.spec.ts, packaged then hosted; Chromium with --autoplay-policy=document-user-activation-required
scenarioMatrix.oracle: With autoplay blocked, B shows 'Enable audio'; one click makes canPlaybackAudio true and the prompt disappears.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: With autoplay allowed, no prompt is shown.
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: Two Chromium launches with different autoplay policies.

scenarioMatrix.name: New controls are accessible and match the approved designs
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: accessibility.spec.ts extended over the new surfaces at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440 in both themes; prometheus-ui-review against the approved shapes
scenarioMatrix.oracle: axe reports no WCAG 2.2 A or AA violation; every control is reachable and operable by keyboard with a fill or elevation focus change of at least 3:1; no borders or outlines; motion stops under reduced motion; the UI review reports no blocking deviation from the approved shapes.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: The axe run fails on a fixture page with a known violation.
scenarioMatrix.evidence: axe JSON, screenshots, UI review findings.

scenarioMatrix.name: Repository rules hold and the other shells still build
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build
scenarioMatrix.oracle: All four commands exit 0; no file over 500 lines; names kebab-case; boundary lint passes; desktop and mobile builds succeed as in web-release WR-9.
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: The line checker fails on a 501-line fixture.

Wall-clock since dispatch (2026-11-18T23:51:55Z) was about 2618 minutes at 2026-11-20T19:30Z against 2700.

boundaryPacket.requiredApprovals: Batch 3: (1) start the boundary run; (2) after the packaged run and reviews, push and open the PR; the operator merges it.
cleanup: Stop and remove the local compose stack
stopConditions: Any gate scenario fails in the packaged run: nothing is pushed
The live digest differs from the merged build
Budget exhaustion: checkpoint + BLOCKED; no further extension, the phase closes unmet with its evidence
boundaryPacket.repairPolicy: A repair is counted only for gate-scenario failures. After one packaged run to completion lists every failing gate scenario, one commit fixes all of them, plus any signal failure known at that time. Signal failures alone never consume a repair.
boundaryPacket.gateRule: The boundary verdict is decided only by the gate scenarios: tasks a person does in a meeting (share, chat, effects, devices, speaker, history, recording, consent, Enable audio, notes) and the accessibility and design-fidelity of the new controls. Each runs end to end through the built images and the browser. Anything else is a recorded signal: it never decides the verdict, never stops the run and never consumes a repair.
signals: pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test (unit): run once, recorded; failures are fixed in the next batched repair if one happens, otherwise listed in the closure
render-gateway-headers.ts --check and the WC-10 header and default-build checks
WC-11 lockfile and versions.toml pin checks
WC-14 repository rules and other-shell builds
